title: Expandable summaries need text
summary: A <summary> element used to expand a <details> section has no text. Put a short visible heading inside it so people know what it opens.
problem: A <summary> element, the clickable heading of a <details> disclosure widget, is empty or holds only an icon with no text alternative. The section expands and collapses, but nothing names the control.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear "disclosure triangle" or "button" with no name, so they cannot decide whether to open it. Voice control users cannot say a name to expand it. Sighted users see a bare marker.
whyItMatters: Expandable sections often hold answers, delivery terms or product details. If the toggle has no name, that content stays hidden from people who cannot guess its purpose. This is a failure of WCAG 4.1.2 at Level A.
steps: Find the <summary> in the scan result and look at what it expands.
Write short text inside it that names the content, such as "Delivery and returns".
If the summary uses an icon, keep the text and mark the icon aria-hidden="true", or add an aria-label to the <summary> as a fallback.
Keep the <summary> as the first child of <details>. Do not nest buttons or links inside it.
after:
Delivery and returns

Orders ship within two working days.
howToCheck: Select the <summary> in the browser accessibility inspector and read its Name. It should match the heading you see. Pressing Enter or Space on it should open the section.
